prompt_stages.codex56_possibility_slate: Invent at least four materially different, original, warm Lost and Found Frequency audio-mystery possibilities from the immutable constraint ingress. The world is ordinary, contemporary or timeless, and human-scale: no speculative technology, ancient artifacts, laboratories, supernatural forces, secret experiments, crime plots, or science-fiction framing. The listed lost possessions remain separate mundane belongings; never combine or reinterpret them as components of a key, artifact, machine, or research specimen. On EVERY possibility, copy the ingress draw's lost_objects array and acoustic_device string VERBATIM into those exact typed fields; do not paraphrase them. Use that mundane device as the only shared cause and culminate in the supplied helpful_ending; do not substitute a storm, outage, crime, or different mechanism. Use string possibility IDs such as p1, p2, p3, p4. Return 4 to 6 possibilities. On EVERY possibility, clue_plan MUST carry one distinct audible clue for EACH lost object in the draw, in the same order, so three lost objects require at least three clue_plan entries. Never merge two objects into a single clue and never leave a lost object without one. Make audible clues occur in fair order. No violence, weapons, blood, threats, cruelty, profanity, smoking, intoxicants, brands, public figures, franchises, adaptations, lyrics, or copied characters. Names must be fictional. Give every possibility one caller per lost object in the callers array -- at least one and at most 6, matching the draw. JSON only.
prompt_stages.codex56_slate_triage: Act as a technical contract checker. Select the one possibility that is most causally solvable through sound and best complies with every safety and originality constraint. selected_possibility_id must be one possibility_id copied verbatim from the supplied slate: never a title, an index, or an invented id. If every candidate carries a concern, select the least compromised one and record the concern in findings. Findings are advisory notes kept with the episode; they never reject a card and never end the run, so always return a selection. Findings must identify concrete fields; do not assign an originality score and do not rewrite prose. JSON only.
prompt_stages.codex56_audible_truth_map: Build the selected possibility into a complete causal truth map. Preserve the ordinary-world Lost and Found Frequency identity: every lost possession remains a separate mundane belonging, the draw's acoustic_device is the only cause, and the supplied helpful ending remains the closure. Never reinterpret the possessions as artifact components, a key, speculative technology, research material, or supernatural evidence. The top level has exactly these fields: title, premise, setting, desk_operator_name, caller_threads, causal_steps, audible_clues, interpretations, reveal, resolution_links. causal_steps, audible_clues, interpretations, and resolution_links are TOP-LEVEL arrays only; never nest them inside caller_threads. required_caller_threads is AUTHORITATIVE and complete: copy EVERY row of it into caller_threads, keeping each thread_id and each lost_object EXACTLY as given -- never shortened, never reworded, never merged, never dropped -- and replace only the caller_name and practical_need placeholders with your own writing. If required_caller_threads has three rows, caller_threads has three rows. Every caller_threads row has exactly thread_id, caller_name, lost_object, practical_need. Give every caller thread at least one audible clue, and create exactly one resolution_links row for every caller thread. Emit only schema-declared fields; never create numbered or suffixed fields such as lost_object_2, lost_object_secondary, or resolution_links_2. Include at least two interpretations: at least one true and at least one plausible false interpretation. Every interpretation must cite at least one existing audible clue ID; clue_ids must never be empty. The listener must be able to solve it before the reveal. Keep the announcer brief and never let the announcer solve the puzzle. JSON only.
prompt_stages.codex56_script_anchor_patch: Return ScriptLinePatch JSON only. targets is authoritative. Return exactly one replacement for every target line_id and no other line IDs. You may rewrite only that line's text. Each replacement text MUST include every required_anchors string verbatim, remain natural spoken dialogue, and preserve the relevant clue or action from current_text. Do not use speaker labels, stage directions, camera language, visual direction, scene/shot instructions, production metadata, or wrappers. Do not change title, line ids, character ids, speakers, line order, score, manifest, music, or any unrequested field. The replacements array holds at least 1 and at most 8 replacements. JSON only.
prompt_stages.codex56_broadcast_score: Design a compact broadcast score from the accepted truth map and grounding_contract. Preserve the ordinary, human-scale Lost and Found Frequency world; no speculative technology, ancient artifact, laboratory, crime, or supernatural substitution. For every lost-object anchor, assign at least one truth-map clue for that object's thread to a non-announcer beat whose intent explicitly names the exact lost-object anchor. The reveal beat's intent explicitly names grounding_contract.device_anchor. The closure beat's intent explicitly names grounding_contract.resolution_anchor. FAIR PLAY: at least one non-announcer clue-carrying beat MUST come BEFORE the reveal beat, and grounding_contract.device_anchor MUST also appear verbatim in the intent of at least one such pre-reveal clue beat -- the device is planted in the clues and only explained at the reveal. The top level has exactly title, premise, setting, cast, scenes, shots, beats, orientation_beat_id, reveal_beat_id, closure_beat_id, opening_music, closing_music. cast, scenes, shots, and beats are separate TOP-LEVEL arrays: never nest shots inside scenes or beats inside shots. Every scene row has exactly scene_id, description, env. Every shot row has shot_id, scene_id, description, visual_prompt, and optional env. Every beat row has exactly beat_id, shot_id, scene_id, char_id, speaker, line_intent. Cast MUST include one separate row with char_id exactly `announcer` and role exactly `announcer`, exactly one different row with role `desk_operator`, and all remaining rows with role `caller`; never combine announcer and desk operator. Use 3-5 fictional cast members, exactly 4 scenes, at least 2 filmable shots, and BETWEEN 5 AND max_beats beats in ordered contiguous shot blocks -- max_beats is supplied with the inputs and is a HARD CEILING, not a suggestion. Every beat becomes one spoken line, so a short broadcast has few beats: tell the whole story, with every clue, inside that budget. Merge beats to fit; never drop a clue to fit. The beats array is chronological and MUST never be reordered. Finish one shot's complete beat block before starting the next: shot_01, shot_01, shot_02 is valid; shot_01, shot_02, shot_01 is forbidden. A later return to an earlier camera setup requires a new shot row with a new unique shot_id for that later contiguous beat run. Before returning JSON, silently scan beats from first to last and verify that every shot_id appears in exactly one adjacent run; if a camera setup returns, mint its new shot row before emitting the score. Also silently scan every line_intent clue_ids array: each truth-map clue ID must occur exactly once across the full beat sequence; retain the first authored placement and remove only a later duplicate. Include typed line intents with truth-map clue IDs, three distinct orientation/reveal/closure beat IDs in that order, and exactly two non-evidentiary music bookends. opening_music and closing_music each have exactly the keys description and generation_prompt; never add music_file, filename, path, cue_id, placement, or other production metadata. Put a non-empty env inside every scene row and a non-empty visual_prompt inside every shot row; never emit schema-path pseudo-fields such as `scenes[*].env` or `shots[*].visual_prompt` at the top level. Every line_intent has exactly the keys intent, arc_phase, and clue_ids. clue_ids is always an array of existing truth-map clue IDs, or [] when that beat carries no clue; never emit singular clue_id. Every line_intent.arc_phase MUST be exactly one of `opening`, `rising`, `reveal`, or `closing`: the orientation_beat_id beat is `opening`, the reveal_beat_id beat is `reveal`, the closure_beat_id beat is `closing`, and every other beat is `rising`. Never use orientation, resolution, closure, climax, or other synonyms as arc_phase values. Assign every truth-map clue to exactly one line intent. Do not write spoken dialogue yet. JSON only.
prompt_stages.codex56_performance_script: Write one complete PerformanceScript for the closed manifest, truth_map, and grounding_contract. Supply exactly one spoken line for every manifest line id and no extras; preserve speaker and character ids. Speak every lost-object anchor naturally on a line carrying a clue for that object's thread. Speak the exact device_anchor on the reveal line and the exact resolution_anchor on the closure line. FAIR PLAY: speak the exact device_anchor ALSO on at least one clue-carrying line BEFORE the reveal line, so the listener hears the device before it is explained; the reveal explains what it meant, it does not introduce it. Preserve the ordinary, human-scale lost-and-found cause; never turn the possessions into an artifact, key, speculative machine, laboratory specimen, crime, or supernatural event. Text must sound natural aloud, contain no labels, wrappers or stage directions, and obey all safety rules. Make clues understandable, voices distinct, the resolution coherent, and the ending helpful. The target word request is advisory; never report counts. The lines array carries at least 5 spoken lines: exactly one per manifest line id, in the manifest's order. JSON only.
